files.content:
# Brief — Sprint & Incident Priority Engine

## Problem
Engineering leads mix feature work and live incidents in one queue. A single unsorted list hides SLA breaches and over-weights easy tasks.

## Target users
Incident commanders and sprint leads who need a ranked queue during a live shift.

## Core behavior
- Score each item as `((impact × 1.6) + (urgency × 1.4)) / sqrt(effort)`.
- When elapsed minutes reach the SLA, add a fixed boost so the breach outranks healthy work of similar size.
- Completing an item drops it out of the breach list without deleting history.

## Files
- `domain.js` — `TaskPriorityEngine` scoring and SLA rules.
- `app.js` — isomorphic facade (`module.exports` and `globalThis.AppCore`).
- `test.js` — Node `assert` suite.
- `index.html` — dark-mode queue you can extend in the browser.

files.author: engine
files.content:
# Runbook — Sprint & Incident Priority Engine

## Layout
1. `domain.js` exports `TaskPriorityEngine`.
2. `app.js` re-exports it for Node and assigns `globalThis.AppCore`.
3. `index.html` loads `domain.js` then `app.js`.
4. `test.js` requires `./app.js` and prints `[PASS]` lines.

## Contract
- `addItem({ title, impact, urgency, effort, slaMinutes, elapsedMinutes })` clamps impact/urgency/effort to 1..10.
- `slaBreached` is `elapsedMinutes >= slaMinutes`. Both values are minutes.
- `getRankedItems` sorts by score descending.
- `getSlaBreaches` returns open items that have already breached.
- Empty titles and unknown ids throw.

## Do not
- Do not compare minutes to milliseconds.
- Do not add npm dependencies.

# Real-Time Engineering Sprint & Incident Priority Engine

A real-time priority engine for engineering sprints that ranks sprint items and incidents using weighted impact/urgency/effort scoring with an SLA breach detector that automatically boosts breached incidents to the top of the queue.

## Features
- Weighted impact/urgency/effort scoring for intelligent prioritization
- SLA breach detector using elapsed minutes against SLA budget
- SLA boost that raises score only after minute budget is spent
- Real-time sprint item storage and ranking

- `brief.md` - Project brief and requirements

- `index.html` - Web UI for the priority engine
- `domain.js` - Core domain logic and scoring engine
- `app.js` - Application wiring and workspace integration
- `test.js` - Verification tests for scoring and SLA logic

## Run
- `node test.js` - Run verification tests
- `open index.html` - Launch the workspace in browser

README.md.content:
# Real-Time Engineering Sprint & Incident Priority Engine

A real-time priority engine for engineering sprints that ranks sprint items and incidents using weighted impact/urgency/effort scoring with an SLA breach detector that automatically boosts breached incidents to the top of the queue.

## Features
- Weighted impact/urgency/effort scoring for intelligent prioritization
- SLA breach detector using elapsed minutes against SLA budget
- SLA boost that raises score only after minute budget is spent
- Real-time sprint item storage and ranking
- Summary counts separating open work from completed items
- Input validation rejecting empty titles and unknown ids

## Files
- `brief.md` - Project brief and requirements
- `runbook.md` - Operational runbook
- `index.html` - Web UI for the priority engine
- `domain.js` - Core domain logic and scoring engine
- `app.js` - Application wiring and workspace integration
- `test.js` - Verification tests for scoring and SLA logic

## Run
- `node test.js` - Run verification tests
- `open index.html` - Launch the workspace in browser

  "briefMd": "# SprintPulse — Real-Time Engineering Sprint & Incident Priority Engine

## 1. Problem
Engineering teams juggle sprint features, bugs, and production incidents with conflicting priorities. Static backlogs fail to surface what matters now: high-impact, urgent, low-effort wins vs SLA-bound incidents about to breach. Managers triage by gut feel, SREs miss SLA clocks, and sprint health is invisible until demo day. Teams need a real-time engine that scores, ranks, and warns — without external tools or setup.

## 2. Target Users
- Engineering Managers & Tech Leads triaging sprint scope daily
- SRE / On-call engineers handling incidents with SLA clocks (4h, 24h, 72h)
- Product Owners balancing impact vs effort for roadmap planning
- Solo devs / small teams needing zero-setup, browser-native prioritization

## 3. Core Features

### A. Weighted Impact / Urgency / Effort Scoring
- Inputs per ticket: impact 1-5, urgency 1-5, effort 1-5 (1=trivial, 5=massive)
- Configurable weights: wImpact default 0.5, wUrgency 0.3, wEffort 0.2 (sum must be 1.0)
- Formula: raw = impact * wImpact + urgency * wUrgency + (6 - effort) * wEffort; score = Math.round(raw * 20) // range 20-100
- Tier mapping: P0 Critical >=85, P1 High >=70, P2 Medium >=50, P3 Low <50
- Real-time recalculation on slider/input change, stable sort by score desc, tie-breaker urgency desc then impact desc
- Weight sliders live-validate sum=1.0 and re-rank instantly

### B. SLA Breach Detector
- Per ticket: createdAt (ISO string or timestamp), slaHours (e.g., 4, 24, 72, 0=none)
- Detector computes: elapsedMs = now - createdAt, remainingMs = slaHours*3600000 - elapsedMs, percentElapsed = elapsedMs / (slaHours*3600000) *100
- Status: safe (<75%), warning (75-99%), breach (>=100% and <150%), critical (>=150% or overdue >24h)
- Batch detector for sprint health: counts breached/warning/safe, healthScore 0-100
- Live ticking every 30s in UI, pure function for tests with injected now param (no Date.now() hardcoding)
- Visual badges + countdown: e.g., 2h 15m left, breached 30m ago, critical styling

### C. Multi-File Workspace
- domain.js: pure, testable domain logic (no DOM, no I/O)
- app.js: dual-mode bridge (Node CommonJS exports + browser window.SprintEngine) + UI controller
- index.html: sleek dark-mode dashboard with ticket form, weight sliders, sortable table, SLA badges, health bar
- test.js: Node assertions covering scoring, ranking, SLA, validation, edge cases; exits 0 on pass
- Data model: Ticket {id, title, type: feature|bug|incident, impact, urgency, effort, slaHours, createdAt, status: todo|in_progress|done, assignee}

## 4. Architecture
- Zero-dependency, vanilla JS (ES5/ES6 compatible), HTML5, CSS3, Node.js for tests
- Flow: UI inputs -> domain.js calculatePriorityScore -> rankTickets -> detectSLABreach -> app.js render -> 30s SLA tick loop
- Persistence: in-memory array + optional localStorage with graceful fallback (try/catch)
- Dual-mode export pattern: if (typeof module !== 'undefined' && module.exports) module.exports = {...}; if (typeof window !== 'undefined') window.SprintEngine = {...}
- Sample data: 6 tickets covering P0-P3, safe/warning/breach/critical states for immediate demo
- Verifiable via node test.js (exit 0) and browser preview via index.html (double-click, no server needed)

- test.js: Node-only test runner using built-in assert. Requires domain.js and app.js, runs deterministic tests, logs pass/fail, exits 0 on pass, 1 on fail.

- rankTickets(tickets, weights) => new sorted array desc by score, tie-breaker urgency desc, then impact desc, stable (do not mutate input).

- validateTicket(ticket) => {valid:boolean, errors:string[]}. Checks title non-empty, impact/urgency/effort 1-5, slaHours >=0, type in allowed.
- filterAndSortTickets(tickets, options) => filtered/sorted array. options: {search:string, type:string, status:string, sortBy:'priority'|'sla'|'createdAt'}

### app.js — Dual-Mode Bridge + UI

### index.html — UI Requirements
- Dark theme: #0f172a bg, #1e293b cards, #334155 borders, #38bdf8 accent, #f8fafc text, Inter/system font, rounded-xl, shadow
- Controls: weight sliders 0-1 step 0.1 with live value + sum indicator (green if 1.0, red else), ticket form (title text, type select, impact/urgency/effort 1-5 selects, slaHours number, assignee text, submit)
- Dashboard: health bar (width = healthScore%), counts (total/breached/warning/safe), filter bar (search, type, status, sortBy)
- Table columns: Title | Type | Impact | Urgency | Effort | Score | Tier Badge (color-coded) | SLA Badge + Countdown | Actions
- Real-time: on any input change, recalc scores and re-rank instantly; SLA badges update every 30s; no page reload
- No external CSS/JS, all inline <style> and <script>, works via file://

- Output: console.log pass/fail per test, final summary, process.exit(0) if all pass else 1

## 3. Do NOT Rules (Strict)
- Do NOT add npm dependencies, package.json, or external CDN links (no fetch, no frameworks)
- Do NOT use fetch, XMLHttpRequest, or backend calls; all in-memory + optional localStorage
- Do NOT use frameworks (React, Vue, etc.) — vanilla JS only, keep bundle <200KB
- Do NOT break dual-mode: app.js must work in both Node (CommonJS) and browser (window) — test with node test.js and file:// index.html
- Do NOT ignore edge cases: invalid inputs, missing slaHours, empty ticket list, future createdAt, zero/negative slaHours, weight sum !=1, NaN, empty title

brief.md.content:
# Brief — Sprint & Incident Priority Engine

## Problem
Engineering leads mix feature work and live incidents in one queue. A single unsorted list hides SLA breaches and over-weights easy tasks.

## Target users
Incident commanders and sprint leads who need a ranked queue during a live shift.

## Core behavior
- Score each item as `((impact × 1.6) + (urgency × 1.4)) / sqrt(effort)`.
- When elapsed minutes reach the SLA, add a fixed boost so the breach outranks healthy work of similar size.
- Completing an item drops it out of the breach list without deleting history.

## Files
- `domain.js` — `TaskPriorityEngine` scoring and SLA rules.
- `app.js` — isomorphic facade (`module.exports` and `globalThis.AppCore`).
- `test.js` — Node `assert` suite.
- `index.html` — dark-mode queue you can extend in the browser.

runbook.md.author: engine
runbook.md.content:
# Runbook — Sprint & Incident Priority Engine

## Layout
1. `domain.js` exports `TaskPriorityEngine`.
2. `app.js` re-exports it for Node and assigns `globalThis.AppCore`.
3. `index.html` loads `domain.js` then `app.js`.
4. `test.js` requires `./app.js` and prints `[PASS]` lines.

## Contract
- `addItem({ title, impact, urgency, effort, slaMinutes, elapsedMinutes })` clamps impact/urgency/effort to 1..10.
- `slaBreached` is `elapsedMinutes >= slaMinutes`. Both values are minutes.
- `getRankedItems` sorts by score descending.
- `getSlaBreaches` returns open items that have already breached.
- Empty titles and unknown ids throw.

## Do not
- Do not compare minutes to milliseconds.
- Do not add npm dependencies.

README.md.content:
# Real-Time Engineering Sprint & Incident Priority Engine

A real-time priority engine for engineering sprints that ranks sprint items and incidents using weighted impact/urgency/effort scoring with an SLA breach detector that automatically boosts breached incidents to the top of the queue.

## Features
- Weighted impact/urgency/effort scoring for intelligent prioritization
- SLA breach detector using elapsed minutes against SLA budget
- SLA boost that raises score only after minute budget is spent
- Real-time sprint item storage and ranking
- Summary counts separating open work from completed items
- Input validation rejecting empty titles and unknown ids

## Files
- `brief.md` - Project brief and requirements
- `runbook.md` - Operational runbook
- `index.html` - Web UI for the priority engine
- `domain.js` - Core domain logic and scoring engine
- `app.js` - Application wiring and workspace integration
- `test.js` - Verification tests for scoring and SLA logic

## Run
- `node test.js` - Run verification tests
- `open index.html` - Launch the workspace in browser
